description: CCLab is a multidisciplinary team whose main mission is to make the world a better place by solving complex technological problems from a social perspective.
summary: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights states that every person has the right to access scientific knowledge. Yet when vital Earth data, such as NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) visualizations of human-driven climate change, is presented only visually, people with visual impairments are excluded from understanding what is happening to our world. To close this gap, we developed EarthPod, an inmersive multisensorial web experience that uses data sonification to turn NASA’s EIC datasets into interactive soundscapes, making Earth science accessible regardless of visual ability, financial situation, or country of origin. Beyond raising awareness of human impact, this approach weaves deep, meaningful connections between listeners and their home, planet Earth.
details:
How EarthPod works?

What benefits does it have?

  • Science turned inclusive: Removes visual barriers from complex scientific data, allowing blind and visually impaired individuals to independently explore and interpret climate information.
  • Deeper bond with our planet: human-inspired sound patterns helps listeners feel long-term environmental changes on an emotional level, inspiring greater care for Earth.
  • Multisensory learning tool: our app benefits not only visually impaired users, but also educators, students, and auditory learners seeking an immersive way to explore Earth science

Intended impact of our project

  • Raise awareness about the impact of human-driven climate change among the visually impaired community through direct, sensory engagement with Earth data.
  • Make scientific knowledge universally accessible and intuitive to everyone, regardless of visual ability, financial situation, or country of origin.

Exploring our creativity

  • Biomimetic sound design: to explain how earth is alive, we designed soundscapes that resemble human vital signs so listeners can truly inmers themselves in the experience.
  • Multisensory experience: we built the app around the expected user experience by advocating for an inclusive approach that translates visual climate data into interactive, navigable soundscapes rather than treating accessibility as an afterthought.

What factors did we consider?

  • Sonification techniques: based on deep reseacher on the sonification subject we succesfully implemented parameter mapping in our project.
  • Computer vision: we translated the colors and physical complexity of the EIC visualisations into parameter values for the sonification technnique.
  • Accessibility for all users: built to strict WCAG 2.2 AA standards with screen-reader support, keyboard navigation, and synchronized audio-visual cues, ensuring universal access for blind, low-vision, and sighted explorers alike.
  • Importance of storytelling: we aim to convey a message about our planet that goes beyond any existing barrier by democratizing scientific knowledge.

Tech stack

  • Programming Languages: Python, TypeScript
  • Core Libraries: pandas (Data), OpenCV and Pillow (Image), Matplotlib (Charts/Graphics), imageio-ffmpeg (Video), wave (Audio - standard library), Streamlit (Graphical User Interface), h5py (HDF5 files)
  • Development Environment: Package manager: uv, IDE: Visual Studio Code (VS Code), Terminal: PowerShell
  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript 6, Vite 8, Wouter, and Zod 4.
  • Accessibility: Strict WCAG 2.2 AA compliance, screen reader support, and testing with axe-core.
  • Multimedia and Graphics: Canvas 2D, Web Audio API, and D3-geo for synchronized visualization and audio.
  • Deployment and Infrastructure: Docker containers, optimized Nginx server, and automated deployment with Kamal 2 and GitHub Actions.
  • Data and Content: Integration of NASA climate data with sonification and speech synthesis (Kokoro-82M).
projectRefs: AI Meets Sonification: Research Agenda and Technology Demonstration
